findings.location: <div class="poem"> stanza 2, line 4 (source.html third line of stanza)
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the Hebrew verb "מרטיב" with a verb that conveys 'showers/portrays abundant outpouring'—for example: "ושופך ברכות מלמעלה," or "ומשפך ברכות מלמעלה," preserving the surrounding HTML.

findings.location: <div class="poem"> stanza 2, line 6 (source.html last line of stanza)
findings.source_quote: Adore and praise our mighty Lord!
findings.suggested_fix: Change the verb "העריצו" (which commonly means 'admire') to a Hebrew verb that conveys worship/adoration in a theological sense: e.g. "השתחוו והשבחו את אדוננו האדיר!" or "עבדו והללו את אדוננו האדיר!" Keep tags and punctuation.

findings.location: <div class="poem"> stanza 2, line 5 (source.html penultimate line of stanza)
findings.source_quote: His mercy reaches down to men-
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the awkward phrasing "רחמיו יורדים לעבר האנשים—" with a more natural rendering that keeps the directional sense, e.g. "רחמיו נשפכים אל בני האדם—" or "רחמיו יורדים אל האנשים—" Keep the dash and HTML.

findings.location: <div class="poem"> stanza 3, line 5 (source.html fifth line of stanza)
findings.source_quote: In wondrous beauty bend the knee;
findings.suggested_fix: Avoid the past-tense/awkward phrasing "בתפארה נפלו ברך;" and use an imperative/present participle that matches the English meter and sense, e.g. "ובתפארה נכרע ברך;" or "בתפארה כפפו את הברך;" Preserve tags and punctuation.

findings.location: <div class="poem"> stanza 3, line 1 (source.html first line of stanza)
findings.source_quote: Give thanks and sing to Christ our King
findings.suggested_fix: The line is mostly correct, but ensure the Hebrew idiom flows: consider "הודו ושירו למשיח מלכנו," (as translated) or optionally "הודו ושירו למשיח, מלכנו" if a slight pause is desired. No HTML structural changes.
